statement: The frame's first out-of-plane mode (duct pods bouncing on the arms) is at or above 200 Hz
rationale: The printed-frame vibration complaint is a soft structural mode low enough to sit inside the flight controller's control loop: the gyro sees it, the PID loop amplifies it, the motors get hot. Betaflight's dynamic notch and gyro low-pass handle a resonance above ~200 Hz with little delay; below ~150 Hz filtering it costs control. Measured by a 2.5D plate FE of the generated layout, hub clamped at the FC posts, motor+prop as point masses (conservative: a free-flying hub moves and raises the mode). REVISED 2026-10-07 from 'arm cantilever frequency above hover motor rotation frequency': that estimate ignored the duct's own mass (it put the arm at 452 Hz; the FE with the ducts on it says ~190 Hz), and the criterion would have failed every commercial whoop frame, which fly well on RPM filtering.
